synthesis.summary: Two intersections emerge: informational gaps are directly tied to purchase intent, and multi-retailer shopping behavior shows cross-channel consideration without strong brand switching.

findings.title: Conversion friction driven by missing basic info (price, where-to-buy, product ID)
findings.business_implication: Interested viewers are pausing at simple missing details; this can reduce click-through and in-store conversion, especially for Mercadona-adjacent personal care items referenced in hauls.
findings.recommended_action_area: Add standardized on-screen info cards and pinned comments with price, SKU/reference, and where-to-buy; ensure captions include brand/model for devices and clarify which items are Mercadona vs Amazon.

findings.title: Cross-retailer purchase path is normal (Amazon + grocers) rather than competitor preference
findings.business_implication: Audiences compare and source products across Amazon and multiple grocers; Mercadona visibility can be strengthened by making its specific item attribution unmistakable within mixed hauls.
findings.recommended_action_area: Creator guidance/briefing: explicitly label Mercadona items (e.g., 'cuchillas de Mercadona') with pack shots and aisle/section cues; consider quick 'Mercadona vs Amazon' callouts only when helpful, not defensive.

synthesis.summary: Two intersections emerge: (1) purchase intent is present but constrained by availability/usability friction; (2) repeated “where to buy / comparison” questions suggest information gaps that can suppress conversion.

findings.title: Conversion interest is present but blocked by availability & usability friction
findings.business_implication: Even motivated viewers may delay or abandon purchases when products are out of stock or perceived as fiddly to assemble, reducing downstream conversion from creator-driven discovery.
findings.recommended_action_area: Retail readiness & product guidance (stock notifications, restock cadence, quick-start/assembly tips).

findings.title: Information gaps (where-to-buy and comparison questions) likely suppress action after discovery
findings.business_implication: Viewers show interest but must ask basic purchase/selection questions, which can slow or prevent purchase decisions—especially when the content triggers impulse interest.
findings.recommended_action_area: Improve description/pinned comment FAQs (buy links/regions, alternatives, aggressiveness/mildness comparison tables).

synthesis.summary: Two cross-dimension intersections stand out: (1) coordinated additive/Yuka callouts creating brand-trust spillover into unrelated posts, and (2) a promising dermaplaning use case that also surfaces usage/safety guidance needs.

findings.title: Additive/Yuka callouts are spilling into unrelated shaving content (template-style)
findings.business_implication: Brand channels can get comment-stream hijacking where product education posts (e.g., shaving) become a venue for broader ingredient/trust activism, potentially degrading campaign message delivery.
findings.recommended_action_area: Community management + issue-routing (pin a response/FAQ on additives/Yuka, triage to customer care, consider moderation policy for off-topic template spam).

findings.title: Dermaplaning/facial-blade use case drives value but needs safety/how-to guidance
findings.business_implication: There is a clear beauty-adjacent use case (peach-fuzz removal to improve makeup) that could expand demand, but minor injury risk suggests a need for better usage education to prevent negative experiences.
findings.recommended_action_area: Content/packaging guidance (prep product, use oil/slip, angle/pressure, hygiene, replacement cadence, warnings).
